Kind is a type of metadata that is used to classify prims in USD and determines the selection behavior in the Viewport. Custom strings can be defined for production pipelines. Kind examples:
  • assembly - an important group model, often a published asset or reference to a published asset
  • group - models that simply group other models.
  • component - a 'leaf model' that can contain no other models
  • model - base class for all model kinds. 'model' is considered an abstract type and should not be assigned as any prim's kind.
  • subcomponent - an identified, important 'sub part' of a component model.

Mesh Attributes
Mesh Topology

What type of meshes to make:
separate vertices: Separate the edge vertices so that they don't get rounded by subdivision.
shared vertices: Share vertices between the body and end caps. If subdivision is turned on, this will produce rounded edges.
separate meshes: Make separate meshes for the body and top/bottom end caps.
xform + separate meshes: Same as separate meshes but all are descendants of a parent xform prim.

What type of normals to make:
none: no normals. This is the default and normals will generally be generated by subdivision.
face-vertex: generate face-vertex normals.

Set how your prims are displayed within the viewer. Note setting a purpose will override the purpose of its descendants. When purpose is set, the viewport display can be filtered by purpose categories.
  • Default: Assign to prims that have no defined purpose that will generally be included in all renders.
  • Render: Assign to prims intended for final high-quality rendering.
  • Proxy: Assign to prims intended for lightweight proxy rendering.
  • Guide: Assign to prims intended as markings, lines, arrows or interaction guides.

When Close Bottom is on and UV Bottom Cap is on, the object's UV patches extend into the bottom cap. When UV Bottom Cap is off, the object's UV patches do not extend onto the cap. Note that when Close Bottom is off, UV Bottom Cap has no effect.

When Close Top is on and UV Top Cap is on, the object's UV patches extend into the top cap. When UV Top Cap is off, the object's UV patches do not extend onto the cap. Note that when Close Top is off, UV Top Cap has no effect.
